title: Chapter 10 — Falconiformes
description: Falcons — swift, agile, pointed-winged birds of prey. DNA analysis revealed they are more closely related to parrots and passerines than to hawks and eagles. The Peregrine is the fastest animal on Earth in a hunting stoop.

children.name: Herpetotheres
children.description: A Neotropical monotypic genus of specialised snake-hunting falcon. The laughing falcon's oversized head and black mask give it an almost comical appearance, but its precision in decapitating venomous serpents is deadly serious.

children.name: Herpetotheres cachinnans
children.description: The laughing falcon (Herpetotheres cachinnans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in subfamily Herpetotherinae of family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Micrastur
children.description: Secretive Neotropical forest falcons built for manoeuvring through dense jungle understorey — short rounded wings and a long tail let them weave through branches in pursuit of lizards, birds, and small mammals. Most species have bare facial skin and are heard far more often than seen.

children.name: Spiziapteryx
children.description: The smallest member of the caracara lineage, this Argentine and Uruguayan endemic resembles a miniature falcon with cryptic grey, white, and black spotted plumage. It hunts insects and lizards from exposed perches in dry woodland and savanna.

children.name: Caracara
children.description: Large, long-legged caracaras of open country, instantly recognisable by their flat-crowned heads, heavy hooked bills, and bare orange-red facial skin. They stride across the ground like corvids, omnivorously scavenging and hunting in a manner unique among raptors.

children.name: Caracara cheriway
children.description: The crested caracara (Caracara plancus) is a bird of prey (raptor) in the falcon family, Falconidae.

children.name: Caracara plancus
children.description: The crested caracara (Caracara plancus) is a bird of prey (raptor) in the falcon family, Falconidae.

children.name: Daptrius
children.description: Two distinctive Neotropical caracaras united by bare facial skin and a taste for wasp brood and fruit alongside carrion and small prey. They are bold, social, and among the noisiest raptors in the Amazon, often encountered in family groups.

children.name: Milvago
children.description: Smaller, paler caracaras of open lowland country, with a more slender build and a less imposing bill than their crested relatives. Both species are bold commensals of human habitation, often seen scavenging around farms, towns, and refuse dumps.

children.name: Milvago chimango
children.description: The chimango caracara (Daptrius chimango), also known as chimango or tiuque, is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Phalcoboenus
children.description: Andean and Patagonian mountain caracaras — robust, long-legged birds of high-altitude grasslands and wind-scoured coasts with striking pied or barred plumage and bare yellow facial skin. They are bold and inquisitive, sometimes approaching hikers in search of scraps.

children.name: Phalcoboenus carunculatus
children.description: The carunculated caracara (Daptrius carunculatus) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Phalcoboenus megalopterus
children.description: The mountain caracara (Daptrius megalopterus), (Spanish: corequenque) is a species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae.

children.name: Phalcoboenus australis
children.description: The striated caracara (Daptrius australis), also known as Forster's caracara, is a Near Threatened bird of prey of the family Falconidae, the falcons and caracaras.

children.name: Falco
children.description: The archetypal birds of prey — streamlined, pointed-winged, lightning-fast. The tomial tooth on the upper mandible severs prey's spinal cord on impact. Five species breed in Sweden regularly, from the hovering kestrel of roadsides to the peregrine reclaiming Stockholm's tower blocks.

children.name: Falco naumanni
children.description: The lesser kestrel (Falco naumanni) is a small falcon.

children.name: Falco tinnunculus
children.description: The common kestrel, also known as the European kestrel, Eurasian kestrel or Old World kestrel, is a species of predatory bird belonging to the kestrel group of the falcon family Falconidae. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".

children.name: Falco newtoni
children.description: The Malagasy kestrel (Falco newtoni), also known as the Madagascar kestrel, Malagasy spotted kestrel, Newton's kestrel, Madagascar spotted kestrel, katiti (Creole) or hitsikitsika (Malagasy), is a small bird of prey of the genus Falco.

children.name: Falco punctatus
children.description: thumb|Showing tail feathers The Mauritius kestrel (Falco punctatus) is a bird of prey from the family Falconidae endemic to the forests of Mauritius, where it is restricted to the southwestern plateau's forests, cliffs, and ravines.

children.name: Falco araea
children.description: The Seychelles kestrel (Falco araeus) is a small bird of prey belonging to the genus Falco in the falcon family, Falconidae.

children.name: Falco moluccensis
children.description: The spotted kestrel (Falco moluccensis), also known as the Moluccan kestrel, is a falcon found throughout Indonesia and Timor-Leste.

children.name: Falco cenchroides
children.description: The nankeen kestrel (Falco cenchroides), also known as the Australian kestrel, is a raptor native to Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Falco sparverius
children.description: The American kestrel (Falco sparverius) is the smallest and most common falcon in North America.

children.name: Falco rupicoloides
children.description: The greater kestrel (Falco rupicoloides) or white-eyed kestrel is a bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco alopex
children.description: The fox kestrel (Falco alopex) is a bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco ardosiaceus
children.description: The grey kestrel (Falco ardosiaceus) is an African bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco zoniventris
children.description: The banded kestrel (Falco zoniventris) is a bird of prey belonging to the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco rupicolus
children.description: The rock kestrel (Falco rupicolus) is a bird of prey species belonging to the kestrel group of the falcon family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco vespertinus
children.description: The red-footed falcon, formerly the western red-footed falcon, is a bird of prey. It belongs to the family Falconidae, the falcons. This bird is found in eastern Europe and Asia although its numbers are dwindling rapidly due to habitat loss and hunting.

children.name: Falco amurensis
children.description: The Amur falcon (Falco amurensis) is a small raptor of the falcon family.

children.name: Falco concolor
children.description: The sooty falcon (Falco concolor) is a medium-sized falcon, breeding from northeastern Africa to the southern Persian Gulf region, and wintering in East Africa (Mozambique, eastern South Africa) and Madagascar.

children.name: Falco columbarius
children.description: The merlin is a small species of falcon from the Northern Hemisphere, with numerous subspecies throughout North America and Eurasia. A bird of prey, the merlin breeds in the northern Holarctic; some migrate to subtropical and northern tropical regions in winter. Males typically have wingspans of 53–58 centimetres (21–23 in), with females being slightly larger.

children.name: Falco femoralis
children.description: The aplomado falcon (Falco femoralis) is a medium-sized falcon of the Americas.

children.name: Falco subbuteo
children.description: The Eurasian hobby, or just hobby, is a small, slim falcon. It belongs to a group of similar falcons often considered a subgenus of Falco.

children.name: Falco cuvierii
children.description: The African hobby (Falco cuvierii) is a small species of bird of prey in the family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco severus
children.description: The Oriental hobby (Falco severus) is a species of falcon typically 27–30 cm long.

children.name: Falco longipennis
children.description: The Australian hobby (Falco longipennis), also known as the little falcon, is one of six Australian members of the family Falconidae.

children.name: Falco berigora
children.description: thumb|A brown falcon used for falconry in Tasmania The brown falcon (Falco berigora) is a relatively large falcon native to Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Falco hypoleucos
children.description: The grey falcon (Falco hypoleucos) is a medium-sized falcon native to Australia, possibly the rarest.

children.name: Falco subniger
children.description: The black falcon (Falco subniger) is a medium-large falcon that is endemic to Australia.

children.name: Falco biarmicus
children.description: The lanner falcon (Falco biarmicus) is a medium-sized bird of prey that breeds in Africa, southeast Europe and just into Asia.

children.name: Falco jugger
children.description: alt=Juvenile laggars are brown birds overall, very similar to juvenile saker falcons Falco cherrug.

children.name: Falco cherrug
children.description: The saker falcon (Falco cherrug) is a large falcon species.

children.name: Falco mexicanus
children.description: thumb|right|A prairie falcon in [[Arizona.]].

children.name: Falco peregrinus
children.description: The peregrine falcon, also referred to simply as the peregrine, is a bird of prey (raptor) in the family Falconidae known for its speed. A large, crow-sized falcon, it has a blue-grey back, barred white underparts and a black head. As is typical for bird-eating (avivore) raptors, peregrine falcons are sexually dimorphic, with females being considerably larger than males.

children.name: Falco pelegrinoides
children.description: The Barbary falcon (Falco peregrinus pelegrinoides) is a non-migratory subspecies of the peregrine falcon found from the Canary Islands eastwards across some parts of North Africa to the Middle East.

children.name: Falco fasciinucha
children.description: The Taita falcon (Falco fasciinucha) is a small falcon found in central and eastern Africa.
